description: Rank member/position groups by their share of all attendance and return the top 10 plus every row tied with the 10th row's share.

b.request: Rank members, grouped by member id and position, by their attendance count as a share of all attendance records (attendance count divided by total attendance rows), and return the top 10 groups by share from highest to lowest, plus any additional groups tied with the 10th group's share, showing member id, position, attendance count, and share
b.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT m.member_id, m.position, COUNT(*) AS attendance_count, CAST(COUNT(*) AS REAL) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM attendance) AS share FROM attendance a JOIN member m ON a.link_to_member = m.member_id GROUP BY m.member_id, m.position), r AS (SELECT g.*, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY share DESC) AS rn FROM g) SELECT member_id, position, attendance_count, share FROM g WHERE share >= (SELECT share FROM r WHERE rn = 10) OR (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM g) <= 10 ORDER BY share DESC

a.request: Matching each attendance record to its member by member id (dropping attendance with no matching member), count the attendance records for each member id and `position` combination, and work out each count as a share of the total of all these counts. List the member id, position, attendance count and share, sorted by share from highest to lowest, and return the top 10 rows, plus any further rows whose share equals that of the 10th row.

c.request: Which are the top 10 members by share of total event attendance? Match attendance to members by member id, count attendance per member id and position, and show the member id, position, attendance count and share of all attendance, from highest share to lowest. Rank member/position groups by their share of all attendance and return the top 10 plus every row tied with the 10th row's share.
c.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT m.member_id, m.position, COUNT(*) AS attendance_count, CAST(COUNT(*) AS REAL) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM attendance) AS share FROM attendance a JOIN member m ON a.link_to_member = m.member_id GROUP BY m.member_id, m.position), r AS (SELECT g.*, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY share DESC) AS rnk FROM g) SELECT member_id, position, attendance_count, share FROM r WHERE rnk <= 10 ORDER BY share DESC, member_id

d.request: Rank each member id and position group by its share of total event attendance, where attendance is matched to members by member id and counted per member id and position. Return the top 10 groups plus any additional rows whose share ties the 10th row's share. Show the member id, position, attendance count and share of all attendance, ordered from highest share to lowest.
d.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT m.member_id, m.position, COUNT(*) AS attendance_count FROM attendance a JOIN member m ON a.link_to_member = m.member_id GROUP BY m.member_id, m.position), s AS (SELECT member_id, position, attendance_count, attendance_count * 1.0 / SUM(attendance_count) OVER () AS share FROM g), r AS (SELECT *, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY share DESC) AS rnk FROM s) SELECT member_id, position, attendance_count, share FROM r WHERE rnk <= 10 ORDER BY share DESC
